appraisal_events.evidence: "vous qui êtes le grand favori, le grand crack comme disent les Anglais"
appraisal_events.explanation: Mme Swann singles the narrator out as Gilberte's greatest favorite among her friends, an explicit compliment on his standing with her daughter.

appraisal_events.evidence: "cet étranger, ce paria que j'avais été et à qui Mlle Swann avançait maintenant gracieusement... un fauteuil délicieux"; "leurs habitudes dont j'avais été trop longtemps exclu... même quand on me fit la faveur de m'y mêler"
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator recalls his own transformation from an excluded stranger, a 'pariah,' barred from the Swanns' intimate world, into someone now habitually welcomed, seated, and folded into their daily life.

appraisal_events.evidence: "cet appartement commun à Odette et à lui qui lui était apparu si inaccessible... ce paradis inespéré... « Madame est-elle prête? » que je lui entendais prononcer maintenant avec une légère impatience mêlée de quelque satisfaction d'amour-propre"
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator observes that Swann now casually possesses the domestic intimacy with Odette that once seemed unattainable to his jealous love, uttering with ease and self-satisfaction words that had once been an inaccessible dream.

status_effects.explanation: Being named Gilberte's greatest favorite gives the narrator local emotional standing in his relation to her.
The narrator crosses from excluded outsider to welcomed, seated member of the Swann household's inner circle, now regularly admitted to their private life.
Swann now holds, with proprietary ease and quiet self-satisfaction, the once-unreachable domestic intimacy with Odette that his earlier jealous love could barely imagine.
